items.evidence: AC#1 test passes and asserts start/combos equal the no-snapshot result, equal expandRange(default open-raise classes, dead) and the typical basis. Holdout: on a different view (CO open, BTN call) 29 hands with VPIP/PFR 70 keeps the default start and 'typical player'; 30 hands switches to observed; hands 0 is typical.

AC#2 passes; it checks differing starts, widthPct = scaledWidthPct(d, o, 30) and start = expandRange(strongestClasses(width), dead) for raiser (PFR) and caller (VPIP), and pins typical d independently. Holdout: on another view the open-raiser width uses PFR and the caller width uses VPIP (formula to 1e-9), start is the strongest-width prefix, o = d still uses the prefix (A-8), width 100 gives every unseen combo, narrowed combos are a subset of start.

AC#3 passes (opponentBasis [{4,40,'based on 40 hands of this opponent'}], repeat call deep-equal). Holdout: 31 and 120 hands give 'based on 31/120 hands of this opponent'; gradeView carries the basis and propagates snapshot RangeErrors.

AC#4 passes (seats [4,6], texts ['based on 45 hands of this opponent','typical player']). Holdout: over 150 random six-max postflop spots the basis list has one entry per live opponent in ascending seat order with the mixed observed/typical split as expected; end-to-end scenario shows the same with real equity.
AC#5 passes (14, 20, 44, 60 to 9 dp). Holdout: scaledWidthPct(30,10,50)=20, (12,80,30)=32.4, cap at n=1000 gives o.

AC#6 passes (width 0, start = 6 AA combos, no ace dead). Holdout: strongestClasses(-5) = {AA}; with hero AcAd and Ah on board the zero-width AA range is fully blocked and falls back to every unseen combo while the basis stays observed (A-5). Note: for a CO open default the zero width comes out 3.6e-15 rather than exactly 0 (see J-1-02, LOW).

AC#7 passes. Holdout: across pot-odds-call, pot-odds-fold, value-raise, value-bet and check-free outcomes (random spots plus an equity sweep facing a bet) the observed explanation starts with the exact lead text including the CONCEPTS definition, equals lead + lower-cased original, keeps the same 1-3 sentence count each ending in .!?; without a snapshot (or when only check-line opponents are observed) no 'opponent type' appears. Base-commit comparison: 123 spots of typical-path recommend output (actions and unseen modes, fixed and real equity) are byte-identical to f64f89c apart from the new opponentBasis key.

Unit 'hand order' tests pass. Holdout: recomputed all 169 class equities with the section 5 rule 7 procedure: 0 mismatches and the sorted order is identical to HAND_ORDER. Justification is 175 words. parseHandOrder rejects null, version 2, non-array hands, a reversed tie (AJo/66), duplicate AA and an Infinity equity, each as RangeValidationError listing the problems. strongestClasses: for prefixes k=1..59 an exact prefix width gives k classes and width+1e-6 gives k+1; across 0..100 the result is always the shortest reaching prefix and monotone; w>=100 gives 169.

Unit validation tests pass. Holdout: RangeError 'Invalid observed stats for seat 6' for hands Infinity, 40.0001, NaN, vpip -0.01, Infinity, '20' and pfr 100.5; invalid entry for a folded seat also rejected; duplicate seat -> 'Observed stats list seat 1 twice'; PFR > VPIP and 0/100 edges accepted; heads-up table with snapshot -> typical, widthPct null; BB check line stays typical.

Unit bots/unseen tests pass. Holdout: adviceOptions drops observedOpponents; unseen mode with an invalid snapshot does not throw and returns all 'typical player'; preflop recommend with a snapshot returns a chart rec without opponentBasis; recommend(view, ACTION_RANGE_ADVICE) typical bases.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected a zero scaled width to be reported as 0. Actual: for default widths other than the AC#6 case (e.g. a CO open-raiser at 100 hands, PFR 0) widthPct is 3.55e-15 due to floating-point in d + (o - d) * 100 / 100. The resulting range is still exactly AA, so behaviour is correct.
findings.fix: Optional: compute the width so that n >= 100 returns o exactly (e.g. weight w = min(n,100)/100 and d*(1-w) + o*w), keeping the formula's values.
